Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the thoughtful conversation. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Pain points / goals you shared:
- You need lower-latency, cost-predictable LLM inference for customer support routing and automated responses.
- Primary blocker: data privacy & logging constraints driven by PCI/PHI adjacent data — must avoid persisting PII and need strong auditability for all admin actions.
- Success criteria: POC demonstrating redaction of PII, configurable retention windows for logs, and an auditable export that your security team can validate.

Current stack (what you told us):
- Front-end support tool + proxy that calls downstream LLM APIs
- In-house logging to Splunk for audit trails
- On-prem KMS for encryption keys (legal wants keys retained in VPC)

What Redwood can provide (high level):
- Configurable retention for request/response logs (per-tenant settings) and data-at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).
- Optional automatic client-side or server-side PII redaction before logs are persisted; ability to disable request/response persistence entirely for sensitive routes.
- Audit log exports and a SOC 2 attestation we can share; support for periodic exports to your S3/secure bucket.

Immediate next steps we agreed on:
1) I’ll share a mutual action plan and our security overview (attached).
2) Marcus (SE) will follow up with a technical note on redaction options and how to wire up your KMS.
3) Schedule a 60-min POC kickoff (we proposed Jul 22) with your Sec/Infra counterparts to capture requirements and access.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (excel), redwood-security-overview.pdf (pdf)

If I missed anything, flag it — otherwise I’ll set the calendar invite for Jul 22 and loop in engineering.

Marissa — thanks for the recap, super helpful. A few clarifications / asks from our side: 

1) Redaction: can Redwood support deterministic redaction on specific fields (e.g., name, SSN, account_number) before anything is stored or forwarded? We prefer redaction at the edge or before any logs reach vendor-managed storage.

2) Retention: our policy requires PII-related logs be deleted within 30 days by default; is per-route/per-model retention configurable from the control plane or does it require a support ticket?

3) Audit logs: we need a way to export a cryptographically verifiable audit trail for admin actions and model rollouts. Can you confirm format and regular export cadence (daily incremental preferred)?

4) KMS: our security team requires customer-managed keys in our cloud account and proof that Redwood cannot access plaintext keys.

I’ve looped in Jake (infra) and legal. Legal will likely send a short questionnaire; we’d like to see your SOC 2 and any pen-test summaries.

If Jul 22 still works, please schedule and include a brief agenda.

Thanks,
Aisha Gupta
Head of Product Security | FinHealth Inc.

Hi Aisha / Jake — thanks for the questions, happy to provide technical detail. Short answers below and happy to expand in the Jul 22 call or in a follow-up tech note.

1) Deterministic redaction: yes — Redwood supports configurable redactors that can be applied at the route or model level. Options:
   - Client-side: your proxy performs regex/PII detection and redacts before sending (recommended for highest assurance).
   - Server-side pre-persist: Redwood can run a redaction pipeline in memory and only persist sanitized logs. We support policy rules (field names/regexes) and can return tokenized placeholders (e.g., <REDACTED_NAME>).

2) Retention controls: retention windows are configurable per-tenant and per-route via the Console. You can change settings in the control plane; changes are audited. If you prefer, we can lock retention via a contract and administer changes through a support-approved flow.

3) Audit logs / verifiability: we provide an append-only admin audit trail with SHA256 hashes for daily snapshots; exports can be delivered to your S3 bucket as newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) or sent to your Splunk/Datadog ingestion endpoint. Incremental daily exports are supported.

4) KMS / key control: we support customer-managed keys (KMS) where encryption/decryption operations happen in your cloud environment via a cross-account integration. Redwood cannot access plaintext keys — only ciphertext references are stored. We can provide architecture diagrams and an integration checklist.

Attachments: data-flow-diagram.png (diagram)

I’ll prepare a short technical note with configuration examples and a sample retention policy (send separately).
